rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test concerns some land game specifically, excluding sea game because sea game is a separate category.
rows.anchor: فخص صيد البر خاصة، ولم يعم الصيد كله؛ لأن للبحر صيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands take small game without weapons, while arrows and spears strike larger game.
rows.anchor: تأخذون صغار الصيد بأيديكم أخذا بغير سلاح، ثم قال سبحانه: { ورماحكم } ، يعنى وسلاحكم النبل والرماح، بها يصيبون كبار الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Hudaibiyya treaty, the Prophet entered Mecca the next year for three days and sacrificed a hundred camels; scavengers came to eat, prompting the sanctuary hunting ban.
rows.anchor: فنحر البدن مائة بدنة، فجاءت السباع والطير تأكل منها، فنهى الله عز وجل عن قتل الصيد فى الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God unseen means abstaining from game while in consecration.
rows.anchor: من يخاف الله عز وجل ولم يره، فلم يتناول الصيد، وهو محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The painful punishment for deliberate hunting after the ban includes painful beating, stripping clothes, and paying compensation; the ruler decides it.
rows.anchor: يعنى ضربا وجيعا، ويسلب ثيابه، ويغرم الجزاء، وحكم ذلك إلى الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu Bishr, named ʿAmr b. Mālik al-Anṣārī, who killed a wild ass while in iḥrām for ʿumra at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أبا بشر، واسمه: عمرو بن مالك الأنصارى، كان محرما فى عام الحديبية بعمرة، فقتل حمار وحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil reads deliberate killing as intentionally killing while forgetting one's state of consecration.
rows.anchor: { ومن قتله منكم متعمدا } لقتله ناسيا لإحرامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compensation applies to intentional or mistaken killing, and when someone points out game and it is killed; it is measured from livestock pairs.
rows.anchor: من الأزواج الثمانية إن كان قتل عمدا أو خطأ، أو أشار إلى الصيد فأصيب، فعليه الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two just, learned Muslim men judge the equivalent livestock compensation.
rows.anchor: يحكم بالكفارة رجلان من المسلمين عدلين فقيهين يحكمان فى قاتل الصيد جزاء مثل ما قتل من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wild ass or ostrich incurs a camel slaughtered in Mecca and given to the poor; neither the hunter nor companions may eat it.
rows.anchor: إن قتل حمار وحش، أو نعامة، ففيها بعيرا بنحره بمكة، يطعم المساكين ولا يأكل هو ولا أحد من أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An antlered deer or ibex incurs a cow for the poor, while birds and pigeons incur a mature sheep or sheep respectively.
rows.anchor: ذوات القرون الأيل والوعل ونحوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pigeon egg incurs one dirham if it contains a chick and half a dirham if it does not.
rows.anchor: وفى بيض الحمام إذا كان فيه فرخ درهم، وإن لم يكن فيه فرخ، فنصف درهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The young of a wild ass or ostrich incurs a matching young camel.
rows.anchor: وفى ولد الحمار الوحش ولد بعير مثله، وفى ولد النعامة ولد بعير مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Young deer or ibex incurs a young cow, while pigeon chicks and fawns incur a young sheep.
rows.anchor: وفى ولد الأيل والوعل ونحو ولد بقرة مثله، وفى فرخ الحمام ونحوه ولد شاة مثله، وفى ولد الظبى ولد شاة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrificial offering reaching the Kaaba is slaughtered in Mecca's sanctuary and fed to Mecca's poor, as in 22:33.
rows.anchor: يعنى ينحر بمكة، كقوله سبحانه فى الحج: ثم محلهآ إلى البيت العتيق [الحج: 33]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food expiation gives each poor person half a ṣāʿ of wheat.
rows.anchor: لكل مسكين نصف صاع حنطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If unable to afford the offering, its price, or feeding the poor, the offender fasts one day per poor person, calculating how many portions the price buys at Meccan food prices.
rows.anchor: ينظر ثمن الهدى فيجعله دراهم، ثم ينظر كم يبلغ الطعام بتلك الدراهم بسعر مكة، فيصوم مكان كل مسكين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden of the deed is the recompense for sin: expiation punishes the offender for killing game.
rows.anchor: يعنى جزاء ذنبه، يعنى الكفارة عقوبة له بقتله الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God pardoned deliberate hunting before this prohibition was revealed.
rows.anchor: تجاوز الله عما صنع فى قتله الصيد متعمدا قبل نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who returns to hunting after the ban faces God's vengeance through beating, ransom, and removal of clothes; God is mighty and avenges disobedience.
rows.anchor: { فينتقم الله منه } بالضرب والفدية وينزع ثيابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says this verse preceded the earlier verse about painful punishment after transgression.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية قبل الآية الأولى: { فمن اعتدى بعد ذلك فله عذاب أليم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sea game is fresh fish and a creature that reproduces only in water; it is lawful for a person in consecration.
rows.anchor: يعنى السمك الطرى، وشىء يفرخ فى الماء لا يفرخ فى غيره، فهو للمحرم حلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food of the sea is salted fish, a benefit for residents and travelers.
rows.anchor: يعنى للمقيم، { وللسيارة } ، يعنى للمسافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Land game is forbidden during consecration; believers must not treat it as lawful and will be gathered for recompense.
rows.anchor: ولا تستحلوا الصيد فى الإحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering to God is resurrection, when people receive recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: فى الآخرة، فيجزيكم بأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples mocked messengers who warned of punishment, denying it would come; Meccan disbelievers mocked Muhammad's warning, and God consoled him to endure their rejection.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله يعزى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليصبر على تكذيبهم إياه بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment the mockers denied eventually encompassed them.
rows.anchor: يعنى فدار { بالذين سخروا منهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel and consider the end of those who denied punishment: destruction; this warns Meccan disbelievers by the fate of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب كان عاقبتهم الهلاك يحذر كفار مكة بمثل عذاب الأمم الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked who owns creation in heaven and earth, the Meccans answered God; Ubayy b. Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd read this as their answer while denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: فردوا عليه فى الرعد، قالوا: الله، فى قراءة أبى بن كعب، وابن مسعود فى تكذيبهم بالبعث، قالوا: الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed mercy for Himself by postponing punishment for them.
rows.anchor: كتب على نفسه الرحمة } فى تأخير العذاب عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will surely gather the Meccans and earlier nations on the certain Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنتم والأمم الخالية، { لا ريب فيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves are defrauded and do not believe that resurrection will occur.
rows.anchor: يعنى لا يصدقون بالبعث بأنه كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny God's signs, meaning the Quran, are deaf to guidance, mute about it, and surrounded by the darkness of shirk.
rows.anchor: صم } لا يسمعون الهدى، { وبكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Banū ʿAbd al-Dār; God leads astray whom He wills and places whom He wills on Islam's straight path.
rows.anchor: عن الهدى، نزلت فى بنى عبد الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those identified among the people placed on the straight path are ʿAlī, al-ʿAbbās, Ḥamza, and Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: منهم: على بن أبى طالب، والعباس، وحمزة، وجعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether people would call on any gods besides God to remove worldly punishment if they truly claimed other gods shared divinity.
rows.anchor: أن يكشف عنكم العذاب فى الدنيا، { إن كنتم صادقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In distress people call on God alone, who removes it if He wills, and abandon the partners they associate with Him.
rows.anchor: وتنسون } ، يعنى وتتركون { ما تشركون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were sent to peoples who denied them like Mecca's disbelievers; God seized those peoples with hardship and adversity so that they might repent and humble themselves.
rows.anchor: لكى { يتضرعون } [آية: 42] إلى ربهم فيتوبون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affliction is hardship and distress; the afflicted should have pleaded to God and repented so He would remove it.
rows.anchor: إلى الله وتابوا إليه لكشف ما نزل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts hardened, meaning dried and did not soften, while Satan made their shirk and denial seem attractive.
rows.anchor: فلم تلن، { وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting the warning means abandoning what the messengers commanded and admonished the earlier peoples to do.
rows.anchor: فلما تركوا ما أمروا به، يعنى وعظوا به، يعنى الأمم الخالية مما دعاهم الرسل فكذبوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After affliction, God opened up every kind of good to them.
rows.anchor: يعنى أنواع الخير من كل شىء بعد الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they rejoiced in what they received and were impressed by their condition, God seized them suddenly at their most secure moment.
rows.anchor: يعنى بما أعطوا من أنواع الخير وأعجبهم ما هم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seized people became mublisūn: held captive and despairing of every good.
rows.anchor: يعنى فإذا هم مرتهنون آيسون من كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting off the people's dābir means eliminating their root; the unjust are associators, and none of them remained.
rows.anchor: يعنى أصل القوم، { الذين ظلموا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds, for destroying His enemies; the warning is directed at Meccan disbelievers.
rows.anchor: فى هلاك أعدائه، يخوف كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage responds to Meccan disbelievers torturing Muslims for Islam and trying to turn them back to disbelief.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن كفار مكة عذبوا نفرا من المسلمين على الإسلام، وأرادوهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot bring benefit or harm in the afterlife, nor harm people in this world; the verse cites 5:76.
rows.anchor: من آلهة، يعنى الأوثان، ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا [المائدة: 76] فى الآخرة، ولا يملك لنا ضرا فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning on one's heels means returning to shirk after God guided the believers to Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى ونرجع إلى الشرك، { بعد إذ هدانا الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy is a bewildered man lured astray by devils while his companions remain on the road and call him to guidance.
rows.anchor: وأصحابه على الطريق يدعونه إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man in the analogy is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Bakr, whom devils misled from guidance.
rows.anchor: فإنه عبد الرحمن بن أبى بكر الصديق، أضلته الشياطين عن الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man's guided companions are his parents, who tell him to come to them; the passage also concerns the one who said 'uff' to his parents, cited as 21:67.
rows.anchor: يعنى أبويه، قالا له: { ائتنا } ، فإنا على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance is Islam, while the deviation the devils invite people to is the religion of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: والضلال الذى تدعونا الشياطين إليه هو الذى أنتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to submit means to be sincere to the Lord of the worlds, and the believers have done so.
rows.anchor: يعنى لنخلص، { لرب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's choosing of the forefathers, descendants, and brothers means selecting them for prophethood; the straight path is Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى واستخلصناهم بالنبوة، { وهديناهم إلى صراط مستقيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referenced divine guidance concerns eighteen prophets from among God's servants, to whom He grants prophethood; shirk would nullify their deeds.
rows.anchor: يعنى ثمانية عشر نبيا، { من عباده } ، فيعطيه النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The books given to the prophets are the book of Abraham, Torah, Psalms, and Gospel; wisdom means knowledge and understanding, alongside prophethood.
rows.anchor: يعنى كتاب إبراهيم، والتوراة، والزبور، والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Meccans disbelieved in the books given the prophets, God entrusted them to people who would not reject them: the people of Medina, the Anṣār.
rows.anchor: يعنى أهل المدينة من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones God guided are the eighteen prophets, and Muhammad is told to follow their sunna.
rows.anchor: يقول للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: فبسنتهم اقتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no wage for belief in the Quran; the Quran is a reminder for all the worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى على الإيمان بالقرآن، { أجرا } ، يعنى جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God's signs means believing the Quran; the instruction to eat what bears God's name answers the Meccan objection about carrion.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالقرآن مصدقين، وذلك أن كفار مكة حين سمعوا أن الله حرم الميتة، قالوا للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans argued that animals they slaughtered themselves should be better than animals God killed; the Muslims answered that God's act is better, and the Meccans challenged their refusal to eat carrion.
rows.anchor: ألا تحدثونا عما قتلتم أنتم بأيديكم أهو أفضل؟ أو ما قتل الله؟ فقال المسلمون: بل الله أفضل صنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made clear that carrion, blood, and pork are prohibited, except when a person is compelled by necessity.
rows.anchor: يعنى وقد بين لكم ما حرم عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many means the Quraysh leaders, who mislead Meccans through uninformed whim about slaughter; God knows the transgressors.
rows.anchor: أهل مكة، { بأهوائهم بغير علم } يعلمونه فى أمر الذبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overt and hidden sin means adultery in public and private; Quraysh condemned public adultery but saw no problem with it in secret.
rows.anchor: يعنى الزنا فى السر والعلانية، وذلك أن قريشا كانوا ينكرون الزنا فى العلانية، ولا يرون به بأسا سرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sin people acquire is shirk, for which they will be recompensed in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يعنى الشرك، { سيجزون } فى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating carrion is disobedience; devils prompt their polytheist allies to dispute with Muslims about slaughter.
rows.anchor: يعنى إن أكل الميتة لمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying the Meccans by deeming carrion lawful makes one a polytheist like them; the verse is linked to 22:67 about each community's ritual and slaughter.
rows.anchor: مثلهم، وفيهم نزلت: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is Islam, and a sound upright religion has no crookedness.
rows.anchor: { دينا قيما } مستقيما لا عوج فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's hanīf stance means sincerity; he was not among the polytheists, meaning Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: يعني مخلصا، { وما كان } إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is ordered out of the Garden and from angelic form into a hideous form; conceit is unfit there, and he is made abased.
rows.anchor: قال: اخرج من صورة الملائكة إلى صورة الدمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis asks to be spared until the last blast, the day Adam and his descendants are raised.
rows.anchor: يعنى النفخة الآخرة، يوم يبعث آدم، عليه السلام، وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respite lasts until an appointed, known term: the first blast.
rows.anchor: فلا تموت إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم، يعني أجلا معلوما، وهي النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's claim that God made him go astray means that God misled him.
rows.anchor: قال: أما إذ أضللتنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sitting on God's straight path means trying to divert people from God's straight religion, Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى لأصدنهم عن دينك المستقيم، يعنى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From in front means the afterlife: Iblis adorns denial of resurrection, Paradise, and Hell.
rows.anchor: من قبل الآخرة، فأزين لهم التكذيب بالبعث، وبالجنة، وبالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From behind means worldly life, which Iblis beautifies and uses to make people withhold its due.
rows.anchor: يعنى من قبل الدنيا، فأزينها فى أعينهم، وأرغبهم فيها، ولا يعطون فيها حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the right is religion: Iblis casts doubt on guidance or beautifies error; from the left are passions, pleasures, and enticing sins.
rows.anchor: من قبل دينهم، فإن كانوا على هدى شبهته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not be grateful, meaning they will not affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: شاكرين } [آية: 17] لنعمتك، فلا يوحدونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Fire ask the people of the Garden for water or food, noting that they know some people on each other's side.
rows.anchor: من الطعام نأكل، فإن فينا معارفكم وفيكم معارفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has forbidden both food and drink to the disbelievers; He raised the Garden's people so the people of the Fire could see their blessings and call to them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله عز وجل رفع أهل الجنة لأهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who take their religion, Islam, as amusement and play neglect it, treat it as falsehood, and enter a religion other than Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى لهوا عنه، ولعبا يعنى باطلا، ودخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life deceived them away from Islam.
rows.anchor: { وغرتهم الحياة الدنيا } عن دينهم الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgetting them means leaving them in the Fire as they abandoned faith in the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فاليوم فى الآخرة نتركهم فى النار، كما تركوا الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs they denied are the Quran, which they claimed was not from God.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالقرآن { يجحدون } [آية: 51] بأنه ليس من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The winds are cloud-spreaders; the cited verse says winds stir clouds, which travel ahead of the winds.
rows.anchor: الرياح نشرا للسحاب، كقوله: يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا [الروم: 48]، يسير السحاب قدام الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind carries heavy, water-filled clouds to barren land with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: يعنى إذا حملت الريح { سحابا ثقالا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As water brings forth all fruits and plants, God brings the dead out of the earth; this sign calls people to recognize resurrection as certain, as also in al-Rūm and al-Malāʾika.
rows.anchor: فتعتبروا فى البعث أنه كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fertile land produces useful plants by its Lord's permission when rained upon.
rows.anchor: فينتفع به كما ينفع المطر البلد الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain on saline, sterile land produces only scant, withered, unhelpful growth; this is like the unbeliever who hears faith but neither professes nor benefits from it.
rows.anchor: فلم ينتفع به، فهكذا الكافر يسمع الإيمان ولا ينطق به ولا ينفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turns the signs in varied matters for people who are grateful, meaning those who affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: فى أمور شتى لما ذكره فى هاتين الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned from the mountain angry and sorrowful over his people's calf worship, of which God had informed him on the Mount.
rows.anchor: يعني حزينا في صنع قومه في عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebuked his people for hastening their Lord's command by rushing the forty-day appointment.
rows.anchor: استعجلتم ميقات ربكم أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses threw the tablets from his shoulder; five were lost and four remained.
rows.anchor: من عاتقه، فذهب منها خمس وبقيت أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seized Aaron by the head and dragged him toward himself; Aaron said the people had overpowered him and nearly killed him, and asked Moses not to let enemies gloat or count him among wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: يعني إلى نفسه، { قال } هارون لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to forgive him and his brother Aaron, to admit them into His mercy, and recognizes Him as most merciful.
rows.anchor: يعني تجاوز عني، { ولأخي } هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calf worshippers incur God's punishment and humiliation, remaining subjugated until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فصاروا مقهورين إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fabricators are those who falsely claimed the calf was their god and Moses's god.
rows.anchor: يعني الذين افتروا فزعموا أن هذا إلهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samiri collected jewelry 35 days after Moses left and fashioned a calf over three days, knowing they would worship it because they had asked Moses for a god like other peoples'.
rows.anchor: وكان السامري جمع الحلي بعد خمسة وثلاثين يوما من يوم فارقهم موسى، عليه السلام، وكان السامري صائغا، فصاغ لهم العجل في ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They worshipped the calf on day 39, and Moses returned the following day at the completion of 40 days.
rows.anchor: فعبدوا العجل لتمام تسعة وثلاثين يوما، ثم أتاهم موسى من الغد لتمام الأربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who committed sins were those who associated partners with God by worshipping the calf; repentance means turning from shirk and believing God is one without partner.
rows.anchor: يعني الشرك الذين عبدوا العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After shirk, God is forgiving and merciful toward them.
rows.anchor: يعني من بعد الشرك، { لغفور رحيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's anger subsided; he took up the tablets after throwing them, and what remained contained guidance from error and mercy from punishment for those who fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: يعني سكن، { أخذ الألواح } بعدما ألقاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received the Torah on Friday, the Day of Sacrifice; unable to carry it, he prostrated and prayed until it was lightened enough to carry on his shoulder.
rows.anchor: وأعطي موسى التوراة يوم النحر يوم الجمعة، فلم يطق حملها، فسجد لله، وجعل يدعو ربه ويتضرع، حتى خففت عليه، فحملها على عاتقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses selected six men from each of twelve tribes, totaling 72; since he was commanded to bring 70, Joshua b. Nun and Caleb b. Jephunneh stayed behind and were promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: من اثني عشر سبطا، ستة ستة، فصاروا اثنين وسبعين رجلا، قال موسى: إنما أمرنى ربى بسبعين رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointment was the forty days; the delegates waited at the mountain's base, then demanded to see God openly, citing 4:153, and were killed by a quake as punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني لميعادنا، يعني الأربعين يوما، فانطلق بهم، فتركهم في أصل الجبل، فلما نزل موسى إليهم، قالوا: أرنا الله جهرة [النساء: 153]، فأخذتهم الرجفة، يعني الموت عقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether God would have destroyed him and the delegates earlier if He wished, before they accompanied him, and worries what to tell Israel after their best people died.
rows.anchor: ما أقول لبني إسرائيل إذا رجعت إليهم وقد أهلكت خيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks whether all are to be destroyed for fools' deeds; he first thinks the foolish ones were those who worshipped the calf, then calls the event God's trial that leads some astray and guides others.
rows.anchor: فهم السفهاء، فقال موسى: { إن هي إلا فتنتك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls God their protector and asks forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: أنت ولينا فاغفر لنا وارحمنا وأنت خير الغافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil says only twelve thousand Israelites worshiped the calf.
rows.anchor: فلم يعبد العجل منهم إلا اثنا عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for good in this world, meaning forgiveness, and in the afterlife, meaning Paradise; turning to God means repentance.
rows.anchor: يعني المغفرة، { وفي الآخرة } حسنة، يعني الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says punishment reaches whom He wills and His mercy fills everything; when Iblis claims inclusion, God specifies those who fear Him, give alms, and believe His signs.
rows.anchor: يعني ملأت كل شيء، قال إبليس: فأنا من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God are monotheists; those who give alms are Muhammad's community, and those who believe the signs accept that the Quran is from God.
rows.anchor: يعني للذين يوحدون ربهم، { ويؤتون الزكاة } ، يعني أمة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Jews claim that they fear God and give alms, God excludes both them and Iblis from the promise described.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود: فنحن نتقي الله، ونؤتي الزكاة، فعزل إبليس واليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger whom his followers describe is Muhammad; al-ummī means he neither reads books nor writes them with his right hand.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني بالأمي الذي لا يقرأ الكتب، ولا يخطها بيمينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is found written in Torah and Gospel; he commands faith as good, forbids shirk as evil, and permits wholesome meat and fat while forbidding carrion, blood, and pork.
rows.anchor: يعني بالإيمان، { وينهاهم عن المنكر } ، يعني الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad lifts prior covenant restrictions on meat, fats, and animals with claws, as well as severe rules requiring execution for intentional and even accidental murder unless the victim's guardian pardons.
rows.anchor: من تحريم اللحوم، والشحوم، ولحم كل ذى ظفر، { و } يضع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { والأغلال التي كانت عليهم } واجبة من التغليظ والتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe Muhammad, assist and support him, and follow the Quranic light revealed with him are successful; Moses asks God to make him part of Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: يعني أعانوه على أمره، { ونصروه واتبعوا النور } ، يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God took Adam's descendants from their backs at Nuʿmān near ʿArafāt and made them acknowledge themselves.
rows.anchor: يقول: وقد أخذ ربك من بنى آدم بنعمان عند عرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rubbed Adam's right back and brought out white descendants like moving specks, then his left and brought out black descendants like specks, comprising a thousand communities.
rows.anchor: مسح صفحة ظهر آدم اليمنى، فأخرج منه ذرية بيضاء كهيئة الذر يتحركون، ثم مسح صفحة ظهره اليسرى، فأخرج منه ذرية سوداء كهيئة الذر، وهم ألف أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Adam these were his descendants and that their covenant required worshipping Him alone without partners, and concerned their provision; Adam assented.
rows.anchor: يا آدم، هؤلاء ذريتك أخذنا ميثاقهم على أن يعبدوني ولا يشركوا بي شيئا وعلى رزقهم، قال آدم: نعم يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asked whether He was their Lord, they answered yes, and the angels witnessed their acknowledgment.
rows.anchor: قال الله للملائكة: اشهدوا عليهم بالإقرار، قالت الملائكة: قد شهدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God invokes this covenant against Arab disbelievers in this world so they cannot claim on Judgment Day that they were unaware of it.
rows.anchor: الميثاق الذي أخذ علينا { غافلين }
